_comment: The phrases a device command has to answer to, in one place.
The desktop matches these in Python (app/desktop_agent.py) and the phone
a phone running standalone has no backend to ask - it is on its own with
the cloud keys stored on it. Two matchers is one more than anybody wants,
but the alternative was the phone answering 'I have no tool that can open
apps on your device' to a request the desktop handles fine.
What must NOT be duplicated is the contract. Both test suites read this
file, so a phrase that works on one and not the other fails a test rather
than being discovered on a phone.
'desktop_only' are things a phone genuinely cannot do - there is no
taking a screenshot of someone else's computer from an Android webview -
and the phone is expected to say so plainly rather than pretend.
_expected_query_note: What each phrase must actually search for, not merely that it searches.
The first version of this contract only asserted the query was non-empty
and did not contain 'youtube'. One of the three matchers captured the
postposition and searched YouTube for 'par' - which passed both of those
assertions. The request looked like it worked and returned the wrong
thing, which is harder to spot than an outright failure.
